title: The Value of Data

header.html: 2. Exploring data transformation with Google Cloud (about 18%)

2.1 Describe the intrinsic role that data plays in an organization's digital transformation: why data is valuable; databases, data warehouses and data lakes; types of data; the data supply chain; data governance; openness and interoperability
the official Google Cloud Digital Leader exam guide

toc.title: Databases, data warehouses and data lakes

html:
1Why data is valuable

Data becomes valuable when it is turned into action.

Value Example
Real-time business insights See sales by store as it happens
Identifying trends Spot seasonal demand before it peaks
Informing strategic decisions Choose where to open the next shop
Fueling AI Train models and ground agents in company data

Organizations can use data they already have, collect new data (sensors, apps, customer interactions) or source data from outside (partners, public data).

Exam tip

. Data is the fuel for analytics and AI. Better data means better decisions and better models.

2Databases, data warehouses and data lakes

Store Holds Best for
Database Current, structured records for applications Transactions: orders, accounts, inventory
Data warehouse Cleaned, structured data from many sources, organized for analysis Reports, dashboards and business intelligence
Data lake Raw data of any type (structured, semi-structured, unstructured) at low cost Data science, machine learning and future uses

3Types of data

Type Meaning
First-party data Your own data about your customers and operations
Second-party data A partner's first-party data that you receive by agreement
Third-party data Data bought or collected by an outside provider
Structured Rows and columns with a fixed schema (tables)
Semi-structured Tags or keys but flexible shape (JSON, XML, logs)
Unstructured No fixed format: images, video, audio, free text, documents

The cloud unlocks unstructured data, which is most of the world's data and was hard to use before.

4The data supply chain

Stage What happens
Data genesis Data is created (a purchase, a sensor reading)
Data collection Data is captured into systems
Data processing Data is cleaned and transformed
Data storage Data is kept in the right store
Data analysis Data is analyzed for insight
Data activation Insight is put to work: a decision, an alert, an AI action
Exam tip

. Genesis, collection, processing, storage, analysis, activation. Activation is where value appears.

5Data governance and openness

Topic Fact
Data governance The policies, roles and processes for data quality, access, security, privacy and compliance across its life
Why it matters Trusted, secure, compliant data is needed for analytics and AI
Data silos Data locked in separate systems that cannot be combined
Openness and interoperability Open formats and standards let data move between platforms, remove silos and avoid vendor lock-in
Exam tip

. Database for transactions, warehouse for analysis, lake for raw data. If a scenario says raw, any type, low cost, future use, the answer is the data lake.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A bank processes customer account transactions all day and needs current, structured records for its apps. Which store fits best?

  • AA data lake of raw files for future research
  • BA data warehouse for yearly reports only
  • CAn image archive for scanned documents
  • DA database for transactional records
Show the answer

Answer: D. Databases hold current structured records for transactional applications.

S2An analyst needs one place with cleaned data from many systems for dashboards and reports. Which store fits?

  • AA data warehouse organized for analysis
  • BA database for application transactions
  • CA message queue for streaming events
  • DA file share for employee documents
Show the answer

Answer: A. A data warehouse holds cleaned, structured data from many sources for analysis.

S3A company wants to keep raw video, text and sensor data cheaply for future machine learning. Which store fits?

  • AA relational database with a fixed schema and keys
  • BA data lake that holds raw data of any type
  • CA data warehouse with strict tables only
  • DA spreadsheet shared by the whole team
Show the answer

Answer: B. A data lake stores raw data of any type at low cost for future use.

S4Customer purchase history that a retailer collected itself is called what?

  • AThird-party data from an outside provider
  • BFirst-party data owned by the retailer
  • CSecond-party data from a partner
  • DUnstructured data without any format
Show the answer

Answer: B. Data you collect about your own customers and operations is first-party data.

S5In the data supply chain, which stage puts an insight to work, for example by triggering an alert?

  • AData collection, which captures the data
  • BData storage, which keeps the data
  • CData processing, which cleans the data
  • DData activation, which uses the insight
Show the answer

Answer: D. Data activation is the final stage, where insight drives action.

S6Why do open standards and interoperability matter for data platforms?

  • AThey make all data public to any company
  • BThey replace the need for data governance entirely
  • CThey force one vendor for every product
  • DThey remove silos and help avoid vendor lock-in
Show the answer

Answer: D. Open formats let data move between platforms, which removes silos and avoids lock-in.

6.2 Recall questions

R1What is a data warehouse for?

Show the answer

Analysis, reports and business intelligence on cleaned data.

R2What does a data lake hold?

Show the answer

Raw data of any type.

R3What is first-party data?

Show the answer

Your own data about your customers and operations.

R4Name the six supply chain stages.

Show the answer

Genesis, collection, processing, storage, analysis, activation.

R5What is data governance?

Show the answer

Policies and roles for data quality, access, security and compliance.

R6What is a data silo?

Show the answer

Data locked in a separate system that cannot be combined.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Value insights, trends, decisions, fuel for AI
Stores database (transactions), warehouse (analysis), lake (raw, any type)
Types first, second, third party; structured, semi-structured, unstructured
Supply chain genesis, collection, processing, storage, analysis, activation
Governance quality, access, security, compliance; openness removes silos and lock-in
